description: Risk and Resilience Strategies of Urban Water Treatment Infrastructure: A Case Study of Yelwa Water Treatment Plant, Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria is a data set listed in DataCite country sweep of research-data repositories (Africa), a research data metadata index, published or maintained by Zenodo. Abstract: Urban water treatment plants (WTPs) are critical infrastructure assets responsible for supplying safe drinking water, yet they remain vulnerable to operational, environmental, and physical disruptions. This study evaluated potential risks, resource availability, and effectiveness of resilience strategies at the Yelwa Water Treatment Plant in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria. Coverage: Nigeria. The portal files it under the publisher Zenodo. Its tags are Risk assessment, resilience strategies, water treatment plant, resource availability, emergency response.. The repository dates the deposit 2026; no later update was checked. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support wastewater and sanitation studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-africa-dc-portal.
